title: Bread and cheese
description: Name the staples, and say what is on the bread.
grammar: gender and articles, and con and sin
grammarNote: Con and sin go straight in front of the noun, and the article stays.

explanation.summary: Bread, cheese and the things you put on them are the words of a simple meal. Con and sin say what is on it and what is not.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: El pan, el queso, el jamón and el chorizo are masculine. La mantequilla, la miel, la tostada and la crema are feminine. La tortilla is the Spanish omelette, and it is not the same word as the tortilla in Mexico. El sándwich takes el because it is stressed on the last syllable.

sections.heading: With and without
sections.body: Con means with and sin means without, and both go straight in front of the noun with no article: pan con queso, café sin leche. The article comes back when you say the thing on its own: el pan con queso, el café sin leche.

items.note: Masculine: el jamón. The accent marks the stress.
Masculine: el sándwich. The accent marks the stress.
Feminine: la tortilla. In Spain this is an omelette.
